Now additionally blocked by P7.2 (Vector[Byte] -> ByteVector). Owning every public codec by hand on top of Vector[Byte] and then swapping representation would mean writing each codec twice, so the representation change goes first. P6f.30's golden fixture is what makes that swap detectable and therefore safe to sequence this way.

When this bead is worked, revisit the P6f.32 decision: with owned codecs, AccountingBatch can carry malformed rows, so accounting can move from fail-the-response to partial-success-naming-the-rows, which is the design deferred on 2026-07-25 because the derived codec could not take an additive field safely.
